LevelIntro: Use rice to learn grinding force. The goal is a soft rice flavor without a burnt taste.
SuccessFeedback: The rice tastes soft and clean, with no burnt flavor.
CloseFeedback: Very close. Adjust the force or grinding time a little.
WrongFeedback: The rice does not taste right. Check the force and grinding time.

LevelIntro: Use tea leaves to learn grinding speed. The goal is gentle tea bitterness followed by sweetness.
SuccessFeedback: The tea tastes balanced: light bitterness first, then sweetness.
CloseFeedback: Very close. Adjust the speed or grinding time a little.
WrongFeedback: The tea is too bitter. Check the speed and grinding time.

LevelIntro: Tutorial complete. Challenge levels begin now. Red bean, dried tangerine peel, and rock sugar each change the dessert at a different moment.
SuccessFeedback: The dessert has a clear order: red bean first, citrus next, sweetness last.
CloseFeedback: Very close. Check the order or grinding time.
WrongFeedback: The dessert tastes out of order. Check when each ingredient is added.

LevelIntro: Peanut and black sesame are both nutty, but each one should keep its own roasted edge. Use New Batch to grind them separately.
SuccessFeedback: Peanut and black sesame stay clear from separate preparation, then join cleanly in the final batch.
CloseFeedback: Very close. Make sure each ingredient is ground alone first, then put both powders together at the end.
WrongFeedback: The nutty flavors need separate preparation followed by one final combined grind.

LevelIntro: White pepper, dried tangerine peel, and ginger are all sharp. Prepare any two together, prepare the remaining spice alone, then combine the prepared powders.
SuccessFeedback: The spices stay clear: one paired powder, one single powder, then one final blend.
CloseFeedback: Very close. Make sure any two spices become one powder, the remaining spice becomes another powder, then the prepared powders meet at the end.
WrongFeedback: The spice batches need a clearer structure: two together, one alone, then the prepared powders together.

LevelIntro: Black sesame should be the strongest flavor without becoming bitter, while glutinous rice keeps the paste smooth. A familiar grain lesson may help.
SuccessFeedback: The Medium amount of black sesame stays clear, the Small amount of glutinous rice softens it, and Medium force keeps the paste balanced.
CloseFeedback: Very close. Check the Medium and Small amounts or the Medium force.
WrongFeedback: The paste is unbalanced. Use Medium black sesame, Small glutinous rice, and Medium force.

LevelIntro: Sand ginger should form the bold base. Keep the familiar citrus accent restrained, and let coarse salt support rather than compete.
SuccessFeedback: The Large amount of sand ginger leads, Small dried tangerine peel adds a restrained citrus note, and Very Small coarse salt supports it under Heavy force.
CloseFeedback: Very close. Check the Large, Small, and Very Small amounts or the Heavy force.
WrongFeedback: The balance is off. Use Large sand ginger, Small dried tangerine peel, Very Small coarse salt, and Heavy force.

LevelIntro: White pepper should stay clear without becoming harsh. Peanut and dried tangerine peel should feel familiar from earlier recipes. Prepare each ingredient in its own batch, then use your Experiment Log to choose the force and speed that fit each one.
SuccessFeedback: Each separate batch preserves its role: white pepper stays clear, peanut adds warmth, and dried tangerine peel keeps the finish light.
CloseFeedback: Very close. Recheck the separate batches and the force and speed used for each ingredient.
WrongFeedback: One or more ingredients were processed the wrong way. Use the Experiment Log to match each separate batch with its suitable force and speed.

LevelIntro: Several familiar ingredients appear again in this zongzi recipe. Prepare red bean, glutinous rice, and black sesame as a single filling batch, adding them in the order suggested by your Experiment Log. Once the filling is ready, add the lotus leaf last and move the pestle briefly to complete the wrapping step.
SuccessFeedback: The zongzi is wrapped neatly: glutinous rice forms the main body, black sesame adds a roasted note, red bean brings gentle sweetness, and the lotus leaf gives it a fresh herbal aroma.
CloseFeedback: Very close. Recheck the filling ratios, the order of the three filling ingredients, or the final lotus leaf wrapping step.
WrongFeedback: The filling is unbalanced or the wrapping step happened too early. Review the ingredient ratios and order, then add the lotus leaf only after the filling is ready.

TargetTasteName: Force Speed Ratio And Order Challenge
LevelIntro: Yangjiang douchi forms the savory base. Ginger, dried tangerine peel, and coarse salt should feel familiar from earlier recipes. Use your Experiment Log to place and balance them, then choose a force and speed that preserve the douchi's depth.
SuccessFeedback: The Large amount of Yangjiang douchi leads the recipe. Ginger adds warmth, dried tangerine peel brightens the finish, and the Very Small amount of coarse salt supports the blend. Heavy force and Slow speed preserve its savory depth.
CloseFeedback: Very close. Recheck one ratio or order step, or the Heavy force and Slow speed used for the whole recipe.
WrongFeedback: The douchi has lost its lead. Review the four amounts and their order, then apply Heavy force at Slow speed to the whole recipe.

LevelIntro: This ginger-scallion sauce brings together lessons from earlier recipes. Sand ginger, ginger, and coarse salt should feel familiar, while scallion white adds a fresh new layer. Use your Experiment Log to decide the amounts, batch structure, order, force, and speed.
SuccessFeedback: The sauce comes together cleanly: the ginger pair forms a bold base, scallion white stays fresh in its own batch, and the Very Small amount of coarse salt finishes the balance. Heavy force and Medium speed bring the ginger batch together.
CloseFeedback: Very close. Recheck one ratio, batch, or order step, or the Heavy force and Medium speed used for the ginger batch.
WrongFeedback: One earlier lesson is out of place. Review the ginger batch, keep scallion white separate, and finish with the Very Small amount of coarse salt.

LevelIntro: This mastery recipe uses only familiar ingredients. Build a douchi-and-ginger base, keep scallion white fresh in its own batch, and let coarse salt finish the sauce. Your Experiment Log contains every rule you need.
SuccessFeedback: Every earlier lesson comes together: douchi leads the first batch, ginger adds warmth, scallion white stays fresh, and the Very Small amount of coarse salt finishes the sauce. Heavy force and Slow speed preserve the savory base.
CloseFeedback: Very close. Recheck one remembered amount, batch, order step, or the Heavy force and Slow speed used for the first batch.
WrongFeedback: One familiar rule is out of place. Review the Experiment Log, rebuild the douchi-and-ginger base, keep scallion white separate, and finish with coarse salt.
